_comment: Curated village profiles. Edit here, then run scripts/06_villages.py to merge computed stats into docs/data/villages.json.

villages.name: Chablis
villages.style: The benchmark for mineral-driven Chardonnay. Steel-fermented purity, flinty nerve, and a salinity that recalls the Kimmeridgian oyster fossils in the soil.
villages.foodPairing: Raw oysters, sashimi, goat cheese, grilled Dover sole
villages.note: The Grand Cru vineyards (Les Clos, Vaudésir) are on another level, but a good village Chablis is one of the best values in all of Burgundy.

climatsOfficial.label: premier cru climats listed by the Bourgogne wine board (BIVB)

villages.name: Petit Chablis
villages.style: Lighter and more straightforward than Chablis proper, planted on Portlandian limestone. Bright, easy-drinking, and refreshingly uncomplicated.
villages.foodPairing: Aperitif, salads, fish and chips, picnic fare
villages.note: Don’t overthink it. This is your Tuesday night white that overdelivers for the price.

villages.name: Puligny-Montrachet
villages.style: The aristocrat of white Burgundy. Laser-focused precision, floral aromatics, and a tension between richness and minerality that defines greatness.
villages.foodPairing: Lobster, turbot in butter sauce, aged Comté, truffle risotto
villages.note: Home to Le Montrachet, arguably the greatest white wine vineyard on earth. Even village-level Puligny has that unmistakable finesse.

villages.name: Chassagne-Montrachet
villages.style: Fuller-bodied sibling of Puligny with more stone fruit and toasted almond character. Shares Grand Cru Le Montrachet but trades some finesse for power.
villages.foodPairing: Roast chicken, cream sauces, grilled langoustines, pork belly
villages.note: Often overshadowed by Puligny, but Chassagne Premier Crus like Morgeot offer incredible depth at slightly gentler prices.

villages.name: Meursault
villages.style: Golden, generous, and open-armed. The poster child for barrel-fermented Chardonnay with buttery texture, nutty warmth, and a round, embracing mouthfeel.
villages.foodPairing: Roast turkey, lobster thermidor, mushroom pasta, Époisses cheese
villages.note: If Puligny is a string quartet, Meursault is a full orchestra. Perrières is the finest Premier Cru here, with almost Grand Cru intensity.

villages.name: Corton-Charlemagne
villages.style: A single Grand Cru appellation on the great hill of Corton. Monumental structure, explosive minerality, and a steely backbone that demands patience.
villages.foodPairing: Seared scallops, foie gras, aged Gruyère, sole meunière
villages.note: Legend has it Charlemagne owned vines here. These wines need 5–10 years to truly open up, but the payoff is extraordinary.

villages.name: Saint-Aubin
villages.style: The insider’s Burgundy. Tucked behind Puligny and Chassagne, offering remarkable finesse and citrus-driven minerality at a fraction of the neighbor’s price.
villages.foodPairing: Grilled fish, crab cakes, asparagus, light pasta dishes
villages.note: The best-kept secret in the Côte de Beaune. Hubert Lamy’s Premier Crus can rival wines costing three times as much from next door.

villages.name: Auxey-Duresses
villages.style: Another hidden valley behind Meursault. Leaner and more angular than its famous neighbor, with a pleasant austerity and good aging potential.
villages.foodPairing: Poached trout, vegetable tarts, mild cheeses, quiche
villages.note: For those who love Meursault’s address but not the price tag. Less opulent, more honest.

villages.name: Pernand-Vergelesses
villages.style: A tiny, charming village on the backside of the Corton hill. Its whites are taut and nervy with green apple freshness and a pleasantly rustic edge.
villages.foodPairing: Charcuterie, escargot, roasted vegetables, simple grilled fish
villages.note: One of the most affordable addresses in the Côte de Beaune. Charming village wines that reward curiosity.

villages.name: Rully
villages.style: Bright and vivacious with a lovely citrus-floral character. Also famous for excellent Crémant de Bourgogne. The gateway to the Côte Chalonnaise.
villages.foodPairing: Aperitif, sushi, goat cheese salad, grilled shrimp
villages.note: Dureuil-Janthial is making some of the most exciting whites in this part of Burgundy. Snag them before prices climb.

villages.name: Montagny
villages.style: White-only appellation with generous, round wines showing ripe orchard fruit and a gentle creaminess. The southernmost outpost of the Côte Chalonnaise.
villages.foodPairing: Roast chicken, cream-based soups, baked brie, white pizza
villages.note: Generous and crowd-pleasing. A great choice when you want something richer without the Côte de Beaune markup.

villages.name: Bouzeron
villages.style: The only village appellation in Burgundy devoted to Aligoté, Chardonnay’s humbler sibling. Racy acidity, stone fruit, and an unmistakable saline finish.
villages.foodPairing: Kir (with crème de cassis), gougères, smoked salmon, aperitif
villages.note: Aubert de Villaine (yes, the Romanée-Conti co-owner) lives here and champions Aligoté. That should tell you something about this grape’s potential.

villages.name: Pouilly-Fuissé
villages.style: The crown jewel of the Mâconnais, recently elevated with Premier Cru vineyards (2020). Rich and concentrated with tropical fruit, toasted notes, and surprising complexity.
villages.foodPairing: Grilled lobster, coq au vin, aged cheddar, risotto with truffle
villages.note: The new Premier Cru status is a game-changer. Top examples rival mid-range Côte de Beaune at better prices, but that window is closing.

villages.name: Saint-Véran
villages.style: Sunny, fruit-forward, and generous. Think ripe peach, white flowers, and a touch of honey. The friendly face of southern Burgundy.
villages.foodPairing: Thai cuisine, grilled vegetables, pizza margherita, brunch
villages.note: One of the best introductions to Burgundy whites. Open a bottle on a warm evening with simple food and you’ll understand immediately.

villages.name: Viré-Clessé
villages.style: Ripe and rounded with orchard fruit and floral notes. A step up from basic Mâcon with more concentration and a touch of elegance from the best sites.
villages.foodPairing: Roast pork, creamy pasta, Brie, lighter curries
villages.note: Jean Thévenet’s old-vine cuvées, made by his son Gautier since 2000, show what this appellation is truly capable of. Burgundy depth, Mâconnais warmth.
